description: Authoritative TS SDK public-surface inventory. Machine-readable, test-validated. Inventory is the source-of-truth for stability levels and change discipline; 007-CLIENT_SDK_GUIDE.md must stay aligned.

changeDisciplineValues.stable-deprecation-first: Breaking changes require a deprecation period. Removal only after at least one minor release with the deprecated API still available and a migration note in the migration ledger.
changeDisciplineValues.provisional-migration-required: Breaking changes are allowed but must be accompanied by a migration note in the migration ledger and a review-visible justification.
changeDisciplineValues.experimental-fast-break: Breaking changes are expected and may happen without prior deprecation. A brief note in the migration ledger is recommended but not enforced by the gate.

subpaths.note: Owns the current shared cancellation/resource-release baseline, the tracing runtime/subscriber baseline, replay signal primitive, shared identity-principal baseline, framework-neutral dependency injection, headless auth-coordination primitives, shared storage contracts, structural utilities, and the dual-layer error bridge: DisposableTrait, CancellationTokenTrait, CancellationTokenSourceTrait, createCancellationTokenSource(), and createLinkedCancellationToken() formalize cooperative cancellation plus owner-side release via dispose(); TimeTrait / createDefaultTimeConfig() formalize the low-level injectable time capability, while IdleCallbackTrait formalizes optional host-owned idle callback capability and EventStreamTrait / EventSubjectTrait remain the SDK-owned reactive primitives even though generic source construction now lives in direct RxJS usage plus the `@securitydept/client/rx` bridge; ReadableReplaySignalTrait / WritableReplaySignalTrait / ComputedReplaySignalTrait, ReplaySignalSlot<T>, ReplaySignalWhenValueOptions, createReplaySignal(), createComputedReplaySignal(), createAndThenComputedReplaySignal(), readonlyReplaySignal(), and isReplaySignalTrait() formalize last-available channels that start empty, replay only emitted values, use get() for synchronous slot reads, and use cancellable whenValue() for asynchronous value waits; SecuritydeptInjectorTrait / SecuritydeptInjector formalize the framework-neutral DI surface, while RequirementPlannerHost (non-serializable behaviour resolved through a parent chain), BaseRequirementPlanner with StaticRequirementPlanner / RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner / MergeRequirementPlanner, the serializable contract (AuthRequirement, RequirementsComposition, resolveEffectiveRequirements, RequirementBehaviour, PipelineStepResult / PipelineRunResult), and runStep() / runUntilSettled() formalize shared auth coordination without a separate core subpath; FoundationEnvironment now treats a root span and tracing runtime as required baseline capabilities, while TracingTrait, createTracing(), TracingEvent, TracingSubscriberTrait, runOperation(), defineInstrumentMethodDecorator(), createTraceTimelineStore() / TraceTimelineStore, and OperationTraceEventType formalize the structured tracing baseline and operation-correlation story; IdentityPrincipal, IdentityPrincipalSchema, IdentityPrincipalWireSchema, parseIdentityPrincipal(), parseIdentityPrincipalWire(), and projectIdentityPrincipal() now formalize the shared human-principal contract and host-facing projection baseline consumed by session/token-set families; ErrorPresentationDescriptor / ErrorPresentationTone / readErrorPresentationDescriptor(), ErrorAttributes, and describeError() remain the host-facing presentation, recovery, and structured error-attribute bridge built on runtime errors.

Owns native Web host adapters and browser-native interop that still depends on page/storage/document concepts: abortSignalToCancellationToken(signal), fromStorageEvent, page lifecycle EventStream source createPageResumeSource, higher-level lifecycle helper createCrossTabSync, native Web host adapters createRouterForNativeWeb(), createPageLifecycleForNativeWeb(), createPopupForNativeWeb(), createEnvironmentForNativeWeb(), and the foundation Web environment boundary centered on `FoundationEnvironment` and `NativeWebEnvironment`. Canonical adopter-facing access is the flattened environment trait object shape (`environment.transport`, `environment.sessionStorage`, `environment.router`, `environment.pageLifecycle`, `environment.popup`, and peers). Raw location/history host objects are adapter inputs only, not core environment fields. Host capabilities are explicit and are not automatic host detection or a DI container.

Owns framework-neutral server host adapters: createTransportForServer() forwards request-scoped headers into a BaseTransportTrait, and createEnvironmentForServer() builds a request-scoped FoundationEnvironment that can be passed directly to package clients such as SessionContextClient.

Owns Web extension background-script host adapters: createRouterForWebExtBackgroundScript(), createStorageForWebExt(), and createEnvironmentForWebExtBackgroundScript(). These adapters translate browser extension tabs/windows/storage APIs and optional browser.runtime.getURL('') into RouterTrait (currentUrl, baseURI, navigate), StorageTrait, and FoundationEnvironment without exposing extension globals to core clients.

Canonical framework-neutral RxJS bridge for SecurityDept event streams and signals. Exposes `toRxObservable(source)` for EventStreamTrait, ReadableSignalTrait, and ReadableReplaySignalTrait, plus `fromRxObservable(observable)` for the reverse bridge. Replay signals do not emit initial empty slots and replay only the last emitted value to late subscribers. `@securitydept/client` remains the event/operator surface; Angular-native signal derivation should use `toNgSignal(source)` from `@securitydept/client-angular`.

Environment-backed BasicAuthContextClient owns zone helpers, boundary observation, login redirect, and logout poison interaction from the root entry. Dedicated ./web and ./server helper subpaths are no longer exported.

React entry is injector-first: it exports `BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT`, `createBasicAuthContextClient()`, and `provideBasicAuthContextClient()` so hosts compose the client through `SecuritydeptProvider`. No domain-specific React Context, Provider component, or `useBasicAuthContext()` lookup hook remains in the public surface.

subpaths.note: Owns the environment-bound SessionContextClient runtime: session state is exposed as signals, lifecycle events as EventStreamTrait, and refresh/logout/redirect operations use FoundationEnvironment transport/router/storage plus span/tracing. No SessionContextController compatibility layer remains.

React entry is injector-first and client-owned: it exports `SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT`, `createSessionContextClient()`, and `provideSessionContextClient()` so hosts compose the SessionContextClient through `SecuritydeptProvider`. No controller token or React Context wrapper remains.

subpaths.note: Owns token-set backend-mode route/client contracts, browser login helpers, and popup callback relay exports. BackendOidcModeClient construction is direct: adopters create a FoundationEnvironment through the appropriate host creator, then call new BackendOidcModeClient(config, environment). Materialized backend clients expose loginWithRedirect({ postAuthRedirectUri }) and loginWithPopup({ popupCallbackUrl }); page navigation is held by the environment's router. relayTokenSetPopupCallbackFromEnvironment() and TokenSetPopupRelayErrorCode are exported from this subpath alongside BackendOidcModeTraceEventType. Backend user-info transport remains a family DTO while its semantic identity-principal parsing/output aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline from @securitydept/client instead of a parallel family-local owner.

Includes the config projection source contract plus the current browser materialization owner: resolveConfigProjection(), networkConfigSource(), ConfigProjectionSourceKind, ClientReadinessState, createFrontendOidcModeWebClientEnvironment(), createFrontendOidcModeBrowserClient(), resolveFrontendOidcModePersistentStateKey(), and resolveFrontendOidcModeBrowserStorageKey(). The canonical browser composition path is createFrontendOidcModeWebClientEnvironment() first, then createFrontendOidcModeBrowserClient({ environment, ...projectionInput }); the materializer requires that explicit environment and does not create default store/fetch/origin dependency fallbacks. Async clientFactory(environment) support remains part of the browser contract, with registry-owned environment passed to client factories instead of scattered sub-capabilities. loginWithPopup() uses popupCallbackUrl as the real OAuth redirect_uri, supports an explicit postAuthRedirectUri for the opener, and is proven by the apps/webui reference host via popup relay plus cross-tab lifecycle browser e2e. FrontendOidcModeTraceEventType keeps popup / callback / refresh / user-info structured trace taxonomy shared and adopter-visible rather than app-local. describeFrontendOidcModeCallbackError() keeps callback-specific host-facing presentation/recovery mapping under the family owner while building on the shared client error presentation descriptor contract. Capability-first layering on the browser path keeps projection endpoint + redirectUri as bootstrap input, the resolved projection as auth-context config, and environment capability wiring explicit. Frontend-mode user-info and metadata principal construction aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline, with app-facing display projection left to shared helper-backed host code.

Token-set-specific orchestration layer: base-client, auth-check trigger event sources, persistence, token-ops, types. Base OIDC clients expose authorizedTransport() from their own environment transport and authorization header signal instead of mode-specific auth-transport wrappers. Auth-check sources are pure EventStream producers; client-owned dispatcher/gateway code submits events into the auth-check runner. The requirement planner host and planner variants are hosted by @securitydept/client. AuthPrincipal aligns to the shared IdentityPrincipal baseline while keeping resource-token facts and substrate ownership outside this human-principal contract.

Framework-neutral multi-client token-set auth registry core. Owns keyed storage, readiness tracking (not_initialized → initializing → ready | failed), canonical lifecycle verbs (`register(entry)`, `unregister(key)`, `resetMaterialization(key)`, `dispose()`), priority=primary|lazy lifecycle, preload / whenReady / idleWarmup, and the reactive registry topology/readiness authority through `state`. Registry lifecycle host capabilities are supplied through `environment`; idle warmup reads `environment.idleCallback` instead of accepting a standalone idle callback option. Omitted-key `whenReady()` and `clientSignalFor()` are single-registered-client conveniences; multi-client hosts must pass an explicit key. `whenReady()` waits for lazy materialization and registry-managed `client.start()` completion. `clientSignalFor(key?)` is the canonical reactive client acquisition API and triggers lazy materialization/start when called; the returned replay signal remains empty until a started client is ready. `registeredKeys()` / `readyKeys()` plus registered snapshot helpers are synchronous convenience over the registry state signal. `createTokenSetOidcAuthRegistry()` now uses the mode client itself as the materialized object; per-client auth state lives on OIDC mode client channels rather than on a service wrapper: replay signals for `authDetermined`, `authSnapshot`, `isAuthenticated`, and `authorizationHeaderValue`, plus plain signals for `lastAuthError` and `authOperations`. Advanced maintenance uses `client.authCheck(options)`; leaf consumers use replay signals instead of registry-level ensure sugar. The subpath also keeps multi-axis discrimination (urlPatterns, callbackPath, requirementKind, providerFamily), lifecycle-safe invalidation errors for stale async materialization, the shared managed OIDC client contracts (`OidcModeClient`, `OidcCallbackClient`), the shared generic callback failure presenter `describeTokenSetCallbackError()`, the callback resume error reader `readTokenSetCallbackResumeErrorDetails()`, and `TokenSetCallbackResumeController` as the shared callback resume state machine. Mode-specific callback copy remains an explicit override owned by the caller or mode package.

Owns focused test observation helpers for the current browser/SDK baseline: FakeClock, FakeTimeConfig, FakeTransport, and InMemoryTraceCollector. Operation-level trace observation through ofOperation(), operationLifecycle(), and assertOperationLifecycle() keeps tests from needing ad hoc operationId filters.

Angular entry keeps provideBasicAuthContext({ config }) as auth-context config only; Angular DI owns host registration, while the service facade stays a thin wrapper over core zone/redirect helpers. Angular DI is the composition root; service methods do not become a second foundation environment API.

subpaths.note: The Angular session adapter is environment-first at the composition root: provideSessionContext({ config }) creates one SessionContextClient-backed service. Initial probing is controlled by SessionContextClientConfig.autoStart or explicit service.start()/refresh().

subpaths.note: React token-set adapter is now injector-first. The root export owns explicit provider factories (`provideTokenSetAuthRegistry()`, `provideTokenSetCallbackResumeController()`), callback bridges (`useTokenSetCallbackResume()`, `TokenSetCallbackComponent`), and React-specific type re-exports on top of the framework-neutral registry core. Ordinary provider composition is scope-owned: `provide...` factories create registry/controller instances inside the current injection context and let `SecuritydeptDestroyRef` own teardown. Advanced hosts that need manual readiness, manual disposal, or custom warmup policy must create and own the registry/controller explicitly before value-providing them. Keyed auth state is read through `useSecuritydeptContext().get(TOKEN_SET_AUTH_REGISTRY)` plus `useReadableSignalValue(service.state)` or through explicit props; no `TokenSetAuthProvider`, fixed runtime bundle, hidden registry/service lookup hook, keyed state hook, or backend-client context helper remains in the public surface.

subpaths.note: Canonical token-set React Query integration surface (not a separate package). `@tanstack/react-query` is an optional peer dependency. This subpath owns cache-key namespacing, readiness queries over registry materialization, and namespace invalidation glue for token-set-aware consumers. Reference-app resource domain models, CRUD transport logic, and groups/entries mutations remain app-local or adopter-local code rather than SDK public surface.

Token-set-specific TanStack Router beforeLoad helper that wraps @securitydept/client-react/tanstack-router and waits for the selected client's `isAuthenticated` replay signal for each route requirement before redirect/block fallback.

Root export owns TokenSetClientRegistryService, multi-client integration, bearer interceptor (BearerInterceptorOptions { strictUrlMatch?: boolean } + TOKEN_SET_BEARER_INTERCEPTOR_OPTIONS InjectionToken; provideTokenSetBearerInterceptor(options?) and createTokenSetBearerInterceptor(registry, options?) accept the same options object — strictUrlMatch: true bounds bearer injection to URLs matching registered urlPatterns), and the canonical Angular route-security builders. TokenSetClientRegistryService is a thin DI wrapper over the shared core ClientRegistry and exposes the same canonical verbs plus signal-state authority. Registry methods materialize and return mode clients; Angular-specific code should bridge client replay signals (`authSnapshot`, `isAuthenticated`, `authorizationHeaderValue`, `authOperations`) with `@securitydept/client/rx` plus `toNgSignal(source)` from `@securitydept/client-angular` when needed rather than using a per-client service wrapper. Angular callback service/component exports have been removed; future Angular callback adaptation should be built over the core token-set registry controller.

Shared React framework bridge with the only SDK-owned React Context. Root exports include `SecuritydeptContext`, `SecuritydeptProvider`, and `useSecuritydeptContext()` for injector access, the context-free interop hooks `useReadableSignalValue()`, `useReplaySignalValue()`, `useInteropObservable()`, and `useEventStream()`, and shared dependency tokens/provider factories such as `ENVIRONMENT` / `provideEnvironment({ environment })` and `AUTH_PLANNER_HOST` / `provideAuthPlannerHost()`. Domain packages compose through this injector bridge instead of publishing additional React Context/Provider APIs.

subpaths.note: Canonical owner of TanStack React Router route-security contract, aligned with Angular's @securitydept/client-angular route metadata contract. Canonical adopter-facing entry: createSecureBeforeLoad() — a beforeLoad-compatible factory that wires root-level runtime policy into TanStack Router execution semantics (throws redirect or RouteSecurityBlockedError). Child routes use withTanStackRouteRequirements() for serializable staticData declaration only. Lower-level building blocks: extractTanStackRouteRequirements (full-route aggregation with merge/replace/inherit), createTanStackRouteSecurityPolicy (headless evaluator), projectTanStackRouteMatches, createTanStackRouteActivator.

Canonical owner of token-set-agnostic Angular framework bridge utilities aligned with @securitydept/client's RequirementPlannerHost / RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner pipeline. Provides: createRouterForAngular(options) (Angular Router → RouterTrait { currentUrl, navigate }); route-metadata projection (projectAngularRouteSegments(leafRoute) → RouteTreeSegment[], plus routeDataFromSegment); route metadata storage in @securitydept/client (SECURITYDEPT_ROUTE_METADATA_KEY / SecuritydeptRouteMetadata / readSecuritydeptRouteMetadata / writeSecuritydeptRouteMetadata); DI planner-host wiring (REQUIREMENT_PLANNER_HOST InjectionToken, provideRequirementPlannerHost(behaviourOrFactory) mapping the Angular DI hierarchy to the host parent chain via skipSelf, injectRequirementPlannerHost()); generic route guards (createAngularCanActivate(options?), createAngularCanActivateChild(options?) bridging RouteCompositionRequirementPlanner and mapping settled→true / blocked→false / redirect→Router.parseUrl); declarative route builders (secureRoute() writes requirement metadata only, secureRouteRoot() writes metadata and attaches canActivate + canActivateChild, optionally registering provideRequirementPlannerHost when a behaviour/host is supplied); and canonical environment DI bridge utilities (provideEnvironment({ environment }), ENVIRONMENT). Framework-neutral RxJS bridging for ReadableSignalTrait/EventStreamTrait lives in `@securitydept/client/rx`; Angular-native signals are derived with `toNgSignal(source)`. ReadableSignalTrait from @securitydept/client remains the canonical signal contract.
